    Match report: Port puts an end to Eagles' winning streak with gutsy scalp

    Port Adelaide has held on for a narrow win over West Coast.

    By Jason Phelan // AFL.com.au
    Oct 10, 2026, 2:55 am
    Listen to audio version of this article
    Sponsored by
    0:00 / 3:32
    Instaread

    ANOTHER stellar performance by Abbey Dowrick propelled Port Adelaide to a tense four-point win against West Coast at Alberton Oval on Saturday.
     
    A week after she claimed the Showdown Medal in the Power’s win against Adelaide, Dowrick was outstanding once again with a game-high 25 possessions and nine clearances.

    The home side led by two points at three-quarter time and clung to a slim lead throughout an enthralling final term, with neither side able to kick a goal, to score a gutsy win that improved its record to 4-5.

    Ella Roberts was the prime mover for the Eagles, who were brave but couldn’t find a way to extend their four-game winning streak.

    The Power had a few chances to seal the result in the nerve-wracking final minutes, but did well to lock the ball in its forward 50 to deny the visitors.

    1 day

    AFLW Highlights: Port Adelaide v West Coast

    The Power and Eagles clash in round nine of the 2026 NAB AFLW Season.

    It was a fitting end to an engrossing duel.

    Despite kicking into a stiff breeze in the first quarter, the Eagles created early scoring chances but let themselves down with poor kicking inside 50.

    The Power was cleaner in attack with disposal efficiency inside 50 of 71.4 per cent to West Coast’s 20.

    Ellie Hampson got on the end of a slick Port transition to poke home the only goal of the term, with the Eagles scoreless in the first quarter for the first time this season.

    Shineah Goody stretched the margin to 13 points early in the second quarter, but her goal would be the home side’s only major of the term.
     
    West Coast came charging back into the contest with two goals in a minute, including a nice snapped major from Bella Lewis after a superb piece of roving, to slice the margin to two points at the main break.
     
    Following on from her second quarter goal, Keeley Skepper doubled her tally with a fine snap in the third term after Dowrick won a clearance and goaled on the run from close range to set up the tense last quarter.

    2 days

    'Star of the competition': Dowrick delivers yet again

    Abbey Dowrick steps up with a crucial major to give Port Adelaide a timely boost.

    Goody gets one up on Eagles star
    Shineah Goody was assigned the tough task of curbing West Coast star Ella Roberts, and the Power midfielder enjoyed a bright patch in the second quarter. Goody went low and hard at the ball, earning a free kick for high contact that she converted from 15m out. However, Roberts got on top in the enthralling duel with a game-high 14 disposals and six clearances in the first half.

    Window open to a tackle or two
    Port Adelaide’s appetite for the contest was clear to see in a lopsided tackle count that the home side led 62-28 at three-quarter time. Piper Window led the charge with nine tackles, with Abbey Dowrick working hard at the coalface with six tackles and a game-high seven clearances at three-quarter time. The trend continued in the last quarter with the Power scoring the gutsy win on the back of a 74-36 tackle count.

    Up next
    Port Adelaide is in action again on Saturday, 17 October, the Power taking on Brisbane at Brighton Homes Arena at 4:05pm local time, while the Eagles host Geelong at Sullivan Logistics Stadium at 4:15pm local time on Saturday. 

    PORT ADELAIDE          1.3       2.4       3.5       3.8 (26)
    WEST COAST               0.0       2.2       3.3       3.4 (22)

    GOALS
    Port Adelaide: Goody, Hampson, Dowrick
    West Coast: Skepper 2, Lewis

    BEST 
    Port Adelaide: Dowrick, Germech, Scholz, Heads, Woodlands, Boag
    West Coast: Roberts, Lewis, Thomas, Bushby, Britton, Rowley

    INJURIES
    Port Adelaide: Nil
    West Coast: Nil

    Crowd: 2,626 at Alberton Oval
